subject: A doubt about the addiction by subtraction vignette

messages.author: 5b9f4c138fd9a813
messages.subject: A doubt about the addiction by subtraction vignette
parts:
Hello geomorph community,

I want to ask something about the vignette "addiction by subtraction" by Dr. Collyer.

When explaining about this function: anova(fit.common, error = c("Residuals", "treatment:family", "Residuals"))

It is said: "... However, in our mixed-model ANOVA, we would prefer to calculate the F-value for treatment as MS Treatment / MS Treatment:Family, to determine if the treatment effect is meaningful compared to shape variation among families we sampled randomly and assigned to treatments."

Is there any type of problem/issue when using the default (MS effects/Ms residuals)? 

Should one be concerned about his/her inferences when using the default when testing for shape variation along species or genera, for example? 

Any regards on that is much appreciated, 
--
Diniz Ferreira
Graduando em Ciências Biológicas
Laboratório de Evolução e Genética de Insetos (LEGIN)
DEZG - IB - Universidade Federal de Pelotas

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A doubt about the addiction by subtraction vignette
parts:
Diniz, this is a matter of whether your factors are nested or not. In Mike´s example, the experimental design clearly includes nested factors, which triggers the comment you mentioned. If one is considering the effect of nested factors, then yes, they should be concerned with using the correct reference MS for significance testing.

Hope this helps

Antigoni
